target: the blind benchmark's shape descriptor -- normalised principal inertia, the one row that can see shape
note: The ruling required the mutation that breaks the intrinsic inertia calculation to be killed by the L0 analytic fixture, so the correctness proof does not depend on an external corpus. Both entries below are killed by tools/test_blind.py, which needs no reference bytes. Every entry was run against the real code and observed to fail the named test. Run with: uv run python tools/mutate.py benchmarks/mutations/blind-inertia.json

mutations.name: normalised-by-volume-not-v-to-the-five-thirds
mutations.why: the exponent is the whole point: at unit density inertia scales as length^5, so dividing by V leaves a quantity scaling as length^2 -- a second size check wearing a shape descriptor's name. The closed-form box fixture catches the value, and the scale-free fixture catches it again from the other side, because a box and the same box ten times larger stop agreeing

mutations.name: a-degenerate-candidate-reports-a-number-anyway
mutations.anchor:
if not mesh.is_watertight or not (volume > 0.0):
        return None
mutations.why: an open surface divides by a zero or meaningless volume and the descriptor becomes NaN or infinity, which formats into the report looking exactly like a measurement -- the failure this file exists to avoid

mutations.name: the-shape-row-says-nothing-to-the-reader
mutations.why: the milder form of the defect review caught on this branch: the descriptor is computed and put in the payload, and what the default table prints carries no measurement. A capability the tool has and its reader does not -- and `--json` is the exception, not the interface

mutations.name: an-unavailable-descriptor-formats-anyway
mutations.why: reaching the number-formatting branch with nothing to format is how a `None`, or a traceback, ends up in a column a reader takes for a measurement
